decisions.statement: A question is asked at one path.
A question arrives by POST.
A question is a JSON object.
An answer is a JSON object unless that answer is the bytes a file has.
A body that will not parse is refused rather than read as an empty question.
A question naming no page type is refused.
A key with a value its shape does not allow is refused.
A test named outside the vocabulary is refused by the name that test was given.
A refusal over a test names the key the test stands on.
A refusal says the fault in the question.
An answer to a question carries the count of what matched beside the rows.
An answer carries at most sixty-four million characters of rows.
A question whose rows run past that is refused rather than answered in part.
A refusal for size names how many rows filled the answer and how many matched.
A refusal for size names narrowing the keys, the rows and the page type.
A read is handed in at a path of its own.
A read with neither a path nor a page is refused.
An answer to a read names the commit its bodies were read at.
A read may name the commit it is answered at as a string.
A read naming that commit as anything but a string is refused.
A write is handed in at a path of its own.
A write may state the commit that write read as a string.
A write stating no writer is refused.
A write stating no message is refused.
A write may have pages rather than bodies.
A page a write has names its page type.
A page a write has names its slug.
A page a write carries states its values.
A page a write has may say whether that page merges.
A page a write carries may hand over the bodies its file properties have.
A body is handed over under the key the property is carried as.
A body that is no string refuses the write.
A page a write has states nothing more.
A page a write has is composed into a body before the write is handed on.
A page that will not compose refuses the write.
An answer to a write names the commit that write landed as.
A shape is asked for at a path of its own.
A shape asked for naming no page type is refused.
A file is asked for at a path of its own.
A file is answered as bytes rather than as JSON.
A refusal over a file is a JSON object as every other refusal is.
A file is never asked for by a path.
Nothing here listens.
Nothing here reads a page.
A refusal says whose fault that refusal was.
A write may keep values outside the commit.
A value a write keeps outside the commit names the path it is kept beside.
A page a write composes keeps its values beside the values that write already kept.
An append is handed in at a path of its own.
An answer to an append names the file part the lines landed in.

definition: a question or a write arriving over HTTP, and the answer sent back
